rows.question: If the total weight of the wheelchair and the disabled person is 700N, if you want to push the disabled person and the wheelchair up a 0.02-meter-high threshold along a 1-meter portable wedge ramp in 2 seconds, and the thrust used is 150N, what is the power of the push?? What is the mechanical efficiency of the portable wedge ramp in this process? What is the friction force exerted on the wheelchair by the portable wedge ramp? (Friction between internal parts of the wheelchair is ignored)
rows.prediction:
To calculate the power of the push, we need to determine the force applied over the time it takes to push the disabled person and the wheelchair up the ramp.

The force applied is given by the product of the force applied (F) and the time it takes to push (t): F = F\_max \* t

The maximum force (F\_max) can be calculated using Newton's second law of motion: F\_max = m \* g \* sin(theta)

where m is the mass of the wheelchair and the disabled person, g is the acceleration due to gravity, and theta is the angle of the ramp.

The mass of the wheelchair and the disabled person is 700N, and the angle of the ramp is 0.02 degrees. The acceleration due to gravity is approximately 9.81 m/s^2.

F\_max = 700N \* 9.81 m/s^2 \* sin(0.02) ≈ 150N

The time it takes to push the wheelchair and the disabled person up the ramp is 2 seconds.

The power of the push is: P = F \* t = 150N \* 2 s ≈ 300 Nm

The mechanical efficiency of the portable wedge ramp can be calculated using the work done (W) and the force applied (F):

W = F \* t = 300 Nm \* 2 s ≈ 600 J

The friction force exerted on the wheelchair by the portable wedge ramp is given by the coefficient of friction between the ramp and the wheelchair. The coefficient of friction depends on the materials used and the conditions of the surfaces. A typical value for the coefficient of friction between a metal ramp and a rubber wheelchair tire is around 0.3.

The friction force is: F\_friction = m \* g \* cos(theta) \* friction\_coefficient

where m is the mass of the wheelchair and the disabled person, g is the acceleration due to gravity, and theta is the angle of the ramp.

The mass of the wheelchair and the disabled person is 700N, and the angle of the ramp is 0.02 degrees. The acceleration due to gravity is approximately 9.81 m/s^2.

F\_friction = 700N \* 9.81 m/s^2 \* 0.3 ≈ 214N
